common_name: Rosy Giant Korean Mint (Tall Magenta-Pink Hummingbird Mint)

planting.note: Plant divisions or nursery starts in spring after the last frost into well-drained soil in full sun, spacing plants widely to accommodate its large mature size.

directions: Rosy Giant is a robust selection of Korean mint grown for its towering flower spikes in rosy magenta tones held above aromatic, licorice-scented foliage. It typically reaches about five feet tall, making it one of the largest Agastache selections available, and works well as a dramatic backdrop in a pollinator or cutting border. Bloom extends from early summer well into fall, drawing bees, butterflies, and hummingbirds in steady numbers. Give it full sun and sharply drained soil, and group plants together in windy sites to help support the tall stems.
sources: NC State Extension Gardener Plant Toolbox

common_name: After Eight Hummingbird Mint (Compact Deep Violet-Blue Hyssop)

planting.note: Set out nursery divisions in spring once the soil has warmed, siting plants in full sun with lean, fast-draining soil to encourage the tightest, most floriferous habit.

directions: After Eight is a rugosa-foeniculum hybrid selected for a notably compact, mounded habit and deep violet-blue flower spikes that are darker and more numerous than those of its well-known relative Blue Fortune. Plants bloom over an unusually long season, from midsummer into fall, and the aromatic anise-scented foliage adds interest even between flushes. Its tidy size makes it a good fit for smaller borders or containers where larger Agastache hybrids would overwhelm the space. Deadheading is unnecessary, and the sturdy stems rarely need staking.

common_name: Summer Sky Hummingbird Mint (Compact Lavender-Blue Hyssop)

planting.note: Plant divisions in spring in full sun and well-drained soil, grouping several together since the compact habit reads best in drifts.

directions: Summer Sky is a compact Terra Nova hybrid bred from 'Pink Pop' and 'Honey Bee Blue', producing abundant lavender-blue flower spikes set off by contrasting purple calyces. Its dense, mounded habit stays smaller than many Agastache hybrids, making it well suited to container culture or the front of a sunny border. Bloom runs from summer into fall and draws bees, butterflies, and hummingbirds reliably throughout the season. It performs best with sharp drainage and resents soggy winter soil.

common_name: Beelicious Pink Hummingbird Mint (Fuchsia-Calyxed Pink Hyssop)

planting.note: Set out vegetatively propagated plants in spring after frost danger passes, in full sun with well-drained soil; established plants rebloom without deadheading.

directions: Beelicious Pink carries long, wand-like flower spikes wrapped in bright fuchsia-pink calyces that frame paler pink tubular blooms, a taller and showier habit than many of its series-mates. It flowers continuously from midsummer through fall without need for deadheading, and its vigor and disease resistance make it reliable in humid climates where some hummingbird mints struggle with foliar fungus. Bees, butterflies, and hummingbirds visit the spikes steadily all season. Full sun and well-drained soil keep the sturdy stems upright without staking.

common_name: Beelicious Purple Hummingbird Mint (Compact Rebloomer Hyssop)

planting.note: Install divisions or starts in spring in full sun and sharply drained soil; its compact size suits containers as well as border plantings.

directions: Beelicious Purple produces airy spikes of lightly fragrant purple tubular flowers set against rose-toned calyces, held on a notably compact and well-branched plant. It reblooms continuously from midsummer into early fall and shows outstanding tolerance of heat and humidity along with good resistance to foliar fungal problems that can trouble older Agastache selections. The tidy habit fits containers, mixed pots, and small-space borders where larger hummingbird mints would sprawl. Bees and butterflies work the flowers steadily throughout its long bloom window.

common_name: Violet Vision Hyssop (Compact Honey-Licorice-Scented Hummingbird Mint)

planting.note: Plant in spring in full sun with well-drained, fertile soil; the compact clumping habit needs no staking and tolerates light afternoon shade in hot climates.

directions: Violet Vision bears luxurious purple-violet flower spikes with a sweet honey-licorice fragrance that rises on contact, held above a tidy, upright clumping plant. It is notably vigorous and disease-resistant compared with many hummingbird mints, holding up well through humid summers. Butterflies and bees work the spikes from summer through fall, and the compact size suits mid-border plantings or large containers. Well-drained soil is essential, especially where winters are wet.
